caption: Three steps: tie the band 5 to 7 cm above the wound, twist a stick underneath to tighten until bleeding stops, then tie it off and note the time.
attribution: Original illustration, drawn for this app

caption: Correct hand position for chest compressions: heel of one hand on the center of the chest, the other hand on top, arms straight.
attribution: Photo by Rama, CC BY-SA 2.0 FR, via Wikimedia Commons

section: Choking in Adults and Children Over One Year
caption: Abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich maneuver) on a conscious, choking adult: stand behind them, fist just above the navel, thrust inward and upward.
attribution: U.S. Army Medical Department Center and School, Fort Sam Houston — public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

section: Choking in Infants Under One Year
caption: For a choking infant under one year: never use abdominal thrusts. Alternate back blows and chest thrusts instead, as shown here.
attribution: Illustration by BruceBlaus, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

caption: A splint immobilizes the joint above and below an injury. Shown here on a finger — the same principle (rigid support plus padding, secured but not tight enough to cut circulation) applies to a splinted arm or leg.
